text: Ribes colandina is a currant species native exclusively to Peru. It is distinct from Ribes andicola, which has orange-yellow flowers, as R. colandina has uniformly dark red flowers (with red petals rather than orange-yellow), black fruits instead of yellow ones, and wider, more deeply lobed leaves. This dioecious shrub reaches a height of approximately 1.54 metres (5.1 ft), with dense to moderate tomentosity due to simple, curly trichomes measuring 12 millimetres (0.47 in) long and scattered subsessile glands, particularly on young shoots and the abaxial leaf surface. The petiole is 1,535 millimetres (60.4 in) long and 1 millimetre (0.039 in) wide, with stipules well differentiated and fused to the petiole for 610 millimetres (24 in). Inflorescences are terminal on short lateral shoots (brachyblasts), forming pendent racemes with a 510 millimetres (20 in) peduncle. The flowers are narrowly cyathiform, featuring a very dark red calyx and corolla measuring 4 millimetres (0.16 in) by 35 millimetres (1.4 in), covered by simple hairs 0.2 millimetres (0.0079 in) long; petals are inserted about 1 millimetre (0.039 in) from the base of the hypanthium, while filaments are inserted approximately half that distance. The fruit is spherical, pendulous, black, and 812 millimetres (32.0 in) in diameter, with scattered shortly stalked glands. The species is found in the La Libertad, Cajamarca, Amazonas, Lambayeque, and Piura departments. It replaces R. andicola south of the Ecuadorean border and is widespread in Piura, Lambayeque, Cajamarca, and La Libertad, while the Ancash Region does not support this species, where it is replaced by R. viscosum.
